fusion_ranked_evidence.title: From prison fears to fireworks, Chinese pastor recounts sudden release after Trump's intervention - Houston Chronicle
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: WASHINGTON (AP) — Ezra Jin Mingri was inside a detention center in southern China on the morning of July 3, worrying that he would likely spend at least 15 years behind bars. In the span of 24 hours, Jin was 15 time zones away, digging into an In-N-Out hamburger in Los Angeles and watching fireworks with his family on the eve of Independence Day, marking America's 250th anniversary. He said he was suddenly released after being held since October, then put on a plane to the U.S. after President Donald Trump raised his case with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in May. He is an exceptional case of a high-profile Chinese detainee going free following a U.S. request at a time when Beijing's leadership has only become more unyielding to foreign pressure. Trump, when leaving Beijing in May, told reporters that he brought up Jin's case and that Xi said he would “strongly consider the pastor.” Trump also has vowed to “save our Great Christian population” worldwide.

fusion_ranked_evidence.title: ‘Falling apart’: Trump’s Boeing deal hits turbulence with Beijing - Politico
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: # ‘Falling apart’: Trump’s Boeing deal hits turbulence with Beijing. The Chinese government is insisting on new conditions to the preliminary agreement that President Donald Trump reached with China’s leader Xi Jinping to purchase 200 Boeing aircraft — putting the high-profile deal at risk, according to three people familiar with the Trump administration’s thinking on negotiations. Beijing has surprised the White House with demands for long-term guarantees on the supply of Boeing engine parts, bogging down negotiations, according to the three people. The Boeing agreement was one of the few tangible outcomes of Trump’s Beijing summit with Xi in May, one which the White House touted as a major success. The White House blames Beijing for the delay in finalizing the sale — valued at an estimated $17 billion to $19 billion — saying post-sale maintenance for those jets was not part of the initial understanding the two leaders reached, said another one of the people familiar with the U.S. thinking on negotiations.
